decisions_this_run: Unlink addresses the link by its own id, not (provider, subject). An IdP subject carries '/', '@' or '+'; a subject-in-path route failed to match and returned 404 without reaching the use case, so id-addressing removes the escaping problem.
Re-linking the same (provider, subject) to the same user is idempotent; binding a pair owned by a different account is refused 422 rather than silently rebinding another user's login.
Unlink revokes only the sessions minted from that exact (provider, subject), in the same transaction, so a live cookie from the removed link cannot outlive it.
An admin may not link an identity to a more privileged account (403). Linking is a takeover route, so the operation must not escalate.
Test assertions on the identity list are delta-based, not absolute: seeded demo users already carry a `demo` link, so an absolute count asserted the seed rather than the change under test.
